title: Boltzmann’s Approach to Statistical Mechanics
version: arXiv:cond-mat/0105242v1 (2001-05-11; only version); chapter in Chance in Physics: Foundations and Perspectives, Lecture Notes in Physics 574, Springer (2001)
locators: Secs. 1-3 and discussion of reversibility/typicality; arXiv full text inspected
assumptions: Classical microstate evolves under time-reversal-invariant mechanics; macrovariables induce Boltzmann macroregions and entropy S_B=k log phase-volume; probability/typicality is relative to a specified macroregion and measure.
conclusion: Goldstein presents Boltzmannian statistical mechanics as deriving typical macroscopic entropy increase from reversible microscopic dynamics plus a low-entropy macrostate and typicality reasoning. Time-reversal symmetry entails the corresponding two-sided entropy-rise issue for a generic low-entropy macrostate at a time; a one-sided observed arrow requires further temporal boundary information or an alternative cosmological model.
proof_status: Primary full text read for stated conceptual argument; no independent derivation or quantitative reproduction.
dependencies: Boltzmann macrostate entropy, phase-space measure, time-reversal symmetry; this paper is a conceptual exposition, not a cosmological model.
open_questions: Which cosmological macrovariables and measure are physically appropriate in general relativity, and how should the probability conditional on present records be fixed?
relevance: Baseline for separating reversible dynamics, statistical typicality, and a cosmological low-entropy boundary condition.
limits: The account does not uniquely specify gravitational entropy or establish an ontological direction of time. The macroscopic arrow is not objective passage.

title: Is the Hypothesis About a Low Entropy Initial State of the Universe Necessary for Explaining the Arrow of Time?
locators: Secs. 1-2 (Past Hypothesis and central-time alternatives); Secs. 3-5 (toy model, non-normalizable measure, present evidence); Secs. 6-8 (mathematical/evidential/theoretical reasoning and conclusion); Appendix A
assumptions: The standard route posits a low-entropy initial macrostate and typical microstate relative to its macroregion. Alternative Carroll-Chen/Barbour-Koslowski-Mercati models use reversible, measure-preserving/unitary dynamics and an unbounded expanding spatial volume, so entropy has no maximum; their typical histories have a central entropy minimum and arrows pointing away on both sides. The paper's toy model simplifies macrostate to a size variable.
conclusion: Authors argue that central-time models can be mathematically compatible with ordinary two-sided typical entropy increase because their cosmological measure is non-normalizable; they distinguish typical histories predicted by a theory from evidential inference conditioned on present records. This supports model-conditional thermodynamic arrows, not a universal claim that the Past Hypothesis is dispensable or that ontology follows.
proof_status: Primary HTML full text inspected at the listed sections; toy-model formulas and measure argument read but not independently reproduced. The authors explicitly leave further typicality/evidential questions open in the paper.
dependencies: Hamiltonian time reversal and volume preservation, Boltzmann entropy, measure/conditioning choices, Carroll-Chen and Barbour et al. cosmological proposals.
open_questions: Whether an infinite-volume/non-normalizable measure and the chosen observer-conditioning are physically justified; whether actual cosmology belongs to these model classes; whether competing coarse-grainings preserve the result.
relevance: Directly compares a low-entropy boundary-condition explanation with cosmological typicality models, while exposing the distinction between theoretical typicality and empirical/evidential inference.
limits: The toy model is not our universe; a non-normalizable measure does not supply ordinary normalized probabilities without additional choices. No conclusion about passage, determinism, eternalism, or presentism.

title: Singularities and Time-Asymmetry
version: In General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey, eds. S. W. Hawking and W. Israel, Cambridge University Press (1979), pp. 581-638; scan inspected
locators: Chapter 12, pp. 613-615 on gravitational clumping, Weyl curvature, and entropy; pp. 629-632 on the proposed initial-singularity Weyl condition and its tentative status
assumptions: Penrose qualitatively associates gravitational clumping and gravitational entropy with increasing Weyl curvature; early matter/radiation may be close to thermal equilibrium while the initial spacetime geometry is specially constrained. The proposed condition is time-asymmetric and directed at initial, not final, singularities.
conclusion: Penrose proposes a low-Weyl-curvature condition at an initial singularity as a geometric boundary condition intended to account for the special low gravitational entropy and thereby the thermodynamic arrow. He states that no clear-cut integral formula for gravitational entropy was then known and that the hypothesis was vague with multiple possible formulations. It is a proposal, not a theorem or established entropy law.
proof_status: Primary chapter scan read at the cited pages; no independent mathematical verification. Penrose labels the hypothesis tentative and says complete details are not worked out at those locators.
dependencies: Classical general relativity and singularity models; qualitative gravitational entropy/Weyl-curvature correspondence; a time-asymmetric initial boundary condition.
open_questions: Which precise scalar/tensor condition defines WCH across singularity classes; whether Weyl curvature measures gravitational entropy in general; how quantum gravity or nonsingular cosmologies alter the boundary proposal.
relevance: Canonical cosmological proposal linking gravitational entropy and an arrow via an initial geometric constraint.
limits: Weyl curvature is not itself a generally established entropy functional. Even if a low-Weyl boundary condition explains an arrow, it does not select a temporal ontology or establish objective passage.

title: On the Weyl Curvature Hypothesis
locators: arXiv v4 abstract and journal metadata; full proof not inspected
assumptions: Stoica defines a class of quasi-regular singularities with an extended Einstein-equation framework and considers cosmological models in that class.
conclusion: Abstract claims the Weyl tensor vanishes at quasi-regular singularities in the stated framework, including an example generalizing FLRW while relaxing homogeneity and isotropy. This is a conditional mathematical result about that singularity class, not evidence that WCH is a universal physical law or that Weyl curvature is a complete entropy measure.
proof_status: Abstract-level only; theorem, definitions, and proof not audited. Bibliographic authorship/version/journal data checked against original arXiv record.
dependencies: Specific regularity assumptions on degenerate metrics/singularities and Stoica's extended Einstein-equation formulation.
open_questions: How broad is the quasi-regular class physically, how does it compare to generic singularity models, and what entropy interpretation is independently justified?
relevance: Shows that a mathematical vanishing-Weyl result is conditional on a chosen singularity class and must not be conflated with confirming Penrose's physical conjecture.
limits: No proof audit and no empirical or thermodynamic conclusion checked.

title: The ‘Past Hypothesis’: Not even false
version: Studies in History and Philosophy of Modern Physics 37(3) (2006), pp. 399-430
locators: Publisher abstract; article sections 5-9 described there but not read
assumptions: Critiques attempts to identify a low Boltzmann-entropy initial macrostate in classical general-relativistic cosmology; emphasizes that a usable entropy concept and phase-space measure must be defined before probability claims.
conclusion: Earman challenges the received claim that modern cosmology has completed Boltzmann's program: he argues initial Boltzmann entropy may be ill-defined or severely hobbled in relevant GR cosmologies, and that even a well-defined low initial entropy would not alone explain temporally asymmetric behavior of ordinary thermodynamic systems. This attacks a premise/bridge in the standard explanation; it is not a demonstration that no cosmological arrow exists.
proof_status: Author abstract only; the detailed model calculations and argument have not been inspected.
dependencies: General-relativistic cosmology, Boltzmann entropy and measure, cosmological boundary conditions.
open_questions: Which specific GR models make the Boltzmann entropy undefined or inadequate; what alternative entropy/account of local arrows survives those objections?
relevance: Major adversarial predecessor against treating the Past Hypothesis as already well-defined and sufficient in relativistic cosmology.
limits: Abstract is a lead, not verification of the detailed critique; do not present Earman's objections as a settled refutation.

title: Arrow(s) of Time without a Past Hypothesis
version: arXiv:1809.04646v2 (2019-01-10; v1 2018-09-12, v3 2020-07-13); published as a chapter in Statistical Mechanics and Scientific Explanation: Determinism, Indeterminism and Laws of Nature, ed. V. Allori, World Scientific (2020), pages unverified
locators: Secs. 1-4 (PH status, fluctuation/observer-selection problem and typicality); Sec. 5 (Newtonian gravity entropy model); Sec. 6 (relational shape-space comparison); conclusion
assumptions: Compare finite-entropy eternal fluctuation cosmologies, bounded-entropy young-universe models, and eternal unbounded-entropy Carroll/Chen or Newtonian-gravity/shape-space models. Typicality depends on dynamics, macrovariables, and measure. A Boltzmann-brain inference requires a cosmological measure and a rule for conditioning on observers/evidence.
conclusion: Authors argue that an eternal unbounded-entropy model can have typical U-shaped entropy histories and arrows on both sides of a central minimum without a fundamental Past Hypothesis, while finite-entropy fluctuation models face self-location/Boltzmann-brain difficulties. They distinguish this theoretical typicality question from inference from current evidence and from Barbour et al.'s relational gravitational arrow. These are model-based author arguments, not established descriptions of observed cosmology.
proof_status: Primary full text read at stated sections. Newtonian N-body asymptotic results and cited simulations are reported rather than independently reproduced; no proof or simulation audit performed.
dependencies: Carroll-Chen cosmology, Barbour-Koslowski-Mercati shape dynamics, Newtonian N-body gravity, Boltzmann entropy proposal, typicality/observer-conditioning.
open_questions: Is the measure well-defined and physically motivated; does Newtonian N-body gravity represent cosmology; what observer typicality/conditioning is warranted; can empirical observations distinguish these cosmological scenarios?
relevance: Provides a direct comparison of Past Hypothesis, typicality, gravitational entropy, and Boltzmann-brain reasoning while retaining alternatives.
limits: The Newtonian model is not relativistic cosmology; simulation evidence is not a general theorem; typicality does not yield a unique empirical probability without measure and reference-class choices. No ontology conclusion. Coordinator correction 2026-10-20: an earlier version string named Studies in History and Philosophy of Science Part B 69 (2020) as the venue; no record supports that. arXiv listing and PhilSci/library records point to the 2020 World Scientific volume instead.

title: Disturbing Implications of a Cosmological Constant
locators: Secs. 5-6, especially discussion of recurrence, fluctuation rates, anthropic weighting and unusual observer-compatible states
assumptions: Conditional holographic/casual-patch picture with positive cosmological constant, finite de Sitter entropy, recurrence, and statistical weighting over fluctuations. The argument depends on assumptions about cosmological constant, horizon complementarity, observer measures, and what counts as an observer-compatible history.
conclusion: Authors argue their assumptions imply recurrences and raise a typicality problem: observer-compatible fluctuations unlike the standard low-entropy cosmological history can dominate, making our observed history atypical. The paper predates common Boltzmann-brain terminology and does not establish a model-independent Boltzmann-brain theorem.
proof_status: Primary arXiv HTML full text inspected at the cited sections; conceptual conditional argument read, not independently verified. Numerical entropy estimates are reported by authors and are not adopted as facts here.
dependencies: Holographic principle, horizon complementarity, de Sitter finite entropy, Poincare recurrence and anthropic/statistical weighting.
open_questions: Are the causal-patch and finite-dimensional assumptions correct; what is the measure over observers/histories; do later cosmological models avoid the atypical-observer result?
relevance: Early primary source for the observer-typicality problem now often discussed via Boltzmann brains.
limits: Highly conditional theoretical argument; observer measure and cosmological assumptions are contested. It concerns typicality and cosmology, not thermodynamic ontology or objective passage.

title: Spontaneous Inflation and the Origin of the Arrow of Time
locators: arXiv abstract only; model and derivation not inspected
assumptions: Proposes spontaneous eternal inflation as a setting to explain thermodynamic arrow direction; details of cosmological state, measure, typicality, and transition rates need full-text audit.
conclusion: Authors suggest spontaneous eternal inflation may provide an explanation for the thermodynamic arrow. At abstract depth this is only a proposal lead; it cannot establish that no Past-Hypothesis-like condition is needed or that the model is typical under a physically justified measure.
proof_status: Abstract-level; no equations, derivations, or predictions audited.
dependencies: Eternal inflation and cosmological statistical/measure assumptions; see comparison with GTZ 2016 and Lazarovici-Reichert 2018.
open_questions: What measure and boundary assumptions govern the claimed spontaneous inflation; how are Boltzmann-brain/observer typicality objections answered?
relevance: Nearest predecessor for cosmological alternatives to a low-entropy initial boundary condition.
limits: Abstract alone cannot verify the model or its explanatory success. No claim about ontology.

title: Observation of Time Reversal Violation in the B0 Meson System
authors: J. P. Lees et al. (BABAR Collaboration)
locators: arXiv abstract and publication metadata; analysis not audited
assumptions: BABAR uses entangled neutral B meson pairs and compares transitions related by time reversal under the experiment's state-tagging protocol.
conclusion: The collaboration reports direct T-violating parameters in neutral B meson transitions. Therefore the blanket statement that all fundamental dynamical laws are time-reversal invariant is false. This microscopic weak-interaction T violation does not by itself explain the macroscopic thermodynamic arrow or select a temporal ontology.
proof_status: Abstract-level; experimental methods, systematic checks, and statistical analysis not independently audited.
dependencies: Neutral B meson mixing/decay, entanglement, transition-state tagging, weak interactions.
open_questions: What is the quantitative contribution of microscopic T-violating processes to macroscopic irreversibility? The cosmological/thermodynamic arrow question remains separate.
relevance: Empirical counterexample to overgeneralized claims about time-reversal symmetry of all dynamical laws.
limits: A particle-transition asymmetry is not the thermodynamic arrow; abstract-only and no ontology consequence.

title: Gravity, Entropy, and Cosmology: In Search of Clarity
version: arXiv:0907.0659v1 (2009-07-03); British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 61(3) (2010), pp. 513-540
locators: Secs. 2-4, 7, 8-10 of primary HTML read by a subsequent reviewer in this task; Sec. 7, “Entropy increase from gravitation and nuclear fusion,” contains the matter-entropy decrease/radiation-compensation claim; key distinctions at Sec. 3 and revised principles/conclusion at Sec. 10. Original worker's earlier screening was abstract-level.
assumptions: Distinguishes gravity's dynamical effects on material macrostates from entropy attributed to gravitational field degrees of freedom. Argues in relevant cosmological regimes that local matter entropy and radiation, expansion-driven departure from equilibrium, and gravitational dynamics must be considered; black-hole entropy is a special case. Scope is the author's statistical-mechanical analysis, not a general quantum-gravity derivation.
conclusion: Wallace argues that collapse need not increase the collapsing matter's entropy: in his model discussion the matter's entropy can decrease while heat/radiation transfer increases total entropy. He says gravitational collapse is not generally the source of local second-law behavior; expansion and nuclear fusion matter to his account. He criticizes Earman's limitations as too strong because gravity can affect material statistical mechanics through dynamics even when field entropy is neglected. This is a substantive counterpoint, not a final resolution of the Past Hypothesis or a universal entropy formula.
proof_status: Primary arXiv HTML sections 2-4, 7-10 read in a subsequent reviewer pass after the initial abstract-only record; the specific matter/radiation statement is located in Sec. 7 (knowledge/audits/fulltext-spotcheck/foundations/findings.jsonl, source_id arrow-wallace-gravity-entropy-2009). Calculations and wider empirical claims not independently reproduced.
dependencies: Classical statistical mechanics of gravitating matter, expanding-universe thermodynamics, matter/radiation entropy, and distinctions between field entropy and dynamical influence.
open_questions: Which parts of Wallace's classical account generalize to broader relativistic/quantum cosmological models; what entropy functional is appropriate for the initial universe; how does the account compare to later gravitational entropy proposals?
relevance: Detailed adversarial counterpoint to both a simplistic Weyl=entropy identification and the claim that Earman's critique rules out cosmological entropy reasoning; also shows why gravitational dynamics can matter without assigning an entropy to the gravitational field.
limits: This is the author's argument in a bounded 2009 treatment; it does not settle all gravitational-entropy questions or establish a unique cosmological entropy. No independent calculation or contemporary model audit.
